the_issuers_routing_ruling.question: The three hand carriers are LGIC_NAMING deliverables and LGIC_NAMING is COMPLETE/CLOSED. Does the re-measure mutate them in place, or land elsewhere?
the_issuers_routing_ruling.ruling: ADDITIVE SIBLINGS, beside each original, in LGIC_NAMING's deliverables. The originals are READ-ONLY and not one byte moves.
the_issuers_routing_ruling.why: THREE reasons, and the first is the binding one. (1) FWD-5's ACCEPT names 'the ranking THE NAMING WORK produced by hand' -- the surface must remain the naming work's, so a re-measure parked in LGIC_ENFORCE's own tree would satisfy the cell and not the outcome. (2) Mutating the originals DESTROYS THE DISCRIMINATOR: the entire content of the 28 'HAND SIDE STALE' findings is the DIFFERENCE between the 2026-09-13 figure and the current one, and an in-place edit deletes the left-hand side of every one of those comparisons. (3) It is this estate's own twice-ruled shape -- RETIRED.md at ENFORCE round 16 and DRIFT_CAUSES.md at LGCTFM round 10, both additive siblings that changed no pinned blob and were found decisive by the grader precisely because they did not.
the_issuers_routing_ruling.grant_mechanics_checked_at_the_cut: A file directly under deliverables/ with no <SERIAL> folder matches NOTHING in the tree-deliverables lane and stays refused (.tools/owned-paths-validate.py:102-103, read at the cut). The worker reaches these paths ONLY through worker_grant -- the fifth additive clause -- which admits exactly the <paths> this order names. So the grant is explicit and enumerated, never conventional.
the_issuers_routing_ruling.disclosed_not_assumed: This is an L5 routing choice inside the analysis's scope, not a widening of it. It is stated here and in the issuance so 1.0.0_SA_CTO can overrule it cheaply; it is not a gate and nothing waits on it.

the_owner_writer_rule_this_round_carries.sentence: A card's `owner` is the DECIDER and is derived by a read that the reason STATES; where the decider is not `permitted_agents` on the surface the remedy names, the card carries the WRITER too.
the_owner_writer_rule_this_round_carries.scope_here: It binds any card THIS round writes. It is NOT a re-issue of the 1303 -- those need only the additive writer field, which is not this round's work.
the_owner_writer_rule_this_round_carries.the_trap_it_closes: A CITATION TO THE RULE A FIELD VIOLATES IS WORSE THAN NO CITATION, because it certifies the field to every later reader. The 1303 cards cite Rule 22a's 'a row's owner is READ, never guessed' and then never show the read. The tell is not the citation's accuracy -- it is whether the cited rule's TEST was RUN on the field beside it.
